explanation: The family is named after the Ural Mountains, near where many linguists place its homeland. Hungarian and Finnish split so long ago that speakers cannot understand each other.

claims.text: Finnish, Estonian and Hungarian are Uralic languages.
Finnish, Estonian and Hungarian are not Germanic, Slavic or Turkic languages.
The Uralic family is named after the Ural Mountains, near the region where many linguists place its original homeland.
Hungarian and Finnish are not mutually intelligible.

writerNotes: Hard but reasoned: Germanic and Slavic are easy to rule out for players who know these languages sound unlike their neighbours, leaving Uralic and Turkic. Finno-Ugric, a branch of Uralic, is kept out of the options so only one is right. Self-check (9.3): lint run clean; every claim listed with risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where honest; datasets: no pinned dataset covers language families; rival test: Turkic tempts because Hungarian has Turkic loanwords and old links to the steppe; its grammar and core vocabulary are Uralic; volatility evergreen, no time words, nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026; regional: European languages, but the family name has a geographic foothold anyone can use; style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words; myths: no match in myths.json; mystery and encore checks: not applicable to a practice item; doubts: the homeland location is debated, so c3 says 'many linguists'
